title: Token Pack Density and Usability Notes
body:
Context / motivation:
- We keep hitting the same UX tension: users want predictable unit increments (credits/packs) but our unit cost (tokens) has high variance per session due to user behavior and model mix.
- Hypothesis: offering 'token packs' with different density (tokens per pack) + lightweight UX controls (expiry, rollover) can reduce cognitive load and increase conversion vs raw per-token pricing.

Definitions / framing:
- Pack = a purchasable token bundle (e.g., 1k tokens). Density = effective tokens per dollar in the pack after discounts.
- Usability axis: how easy to understand + how likely to match user consumption pattern. Higher density -> better $/token but higher commitment/friction.

Rough unit-econ assumptions (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline hosted inference cost (blended across small/med/large models): ~ $6.50 / GPU-hour equivalent (amortized infra + ops). (NOTE: still rough, need to sync with infra team).
- Effective tokens/sec for typical front-end LLM usage (mixed small+medium): ~ 1,200 tokens/minute = 20 tokens/sec (OBS: depends heavily on model selection; for long-form it's lower).
- If we assume sustained throughput 20 tokens/sec -> per hour = 72k tokens.
- Cost per token (infrastructure only) = $6.50 / 72k ≈ $0.0000903 per token (~0.009 cents).
- Add overheads (API gateway, cache storage, SRE, error amortization) -> apply x2.5 multiplier: end-to-end cost ≈ $0.000225 per token.
- Target gross margin for hosted PAYG product: 70% -> MSRP per token ≈ $0.00075.

Pack pricing examples (density ladder):
- Pocket (low commitment): 1,000 tokens, MSRP = $0.90 (effective $/token = $0.00090) 
- Starter (mid): 10,000 tokens, MSRP = $6.50 (effective $/token = $0.00065)
- Pro (high): 100,000 tokens, MSRP = $50 (effective $/token = $0.00050)

Quick validation vs unit cost:\
- Pocket margin = (0.00090 - 0.000225)/0.00090 ≈ 75%
- Starter margin ≈ 65%
- Pro margin ≈ 55%
- Rationale: smaller packs should have higher margin to offset friction/transaction cost and prevent arbitrage. Larger packs trade margin for lock-in.

Behavioral / UX considerations:
- Perceived simplicity: round numbers (1k, 10k) preferred. Show ‘‘equivalent messages’’ examples (e.g., 1k tokens ≈ 10 short prompts or 1 long convo).
- Expiry: expiration increases urgency but hurts long-term fairness. Options: 12 months expiry for Pocket, 24 months for Starter/Pro, with rollover capped at 2x last-purchase pack.
- Auto-refill/subscribe UX: make it opt-in; show forecasted usage and recommend pack size when an account approaches 60% of balance.
- Recovery/fraud: small packs are easier to refund; big packs should have stronger anti-fraud checks (KYB for large purchases).

Pack density mechanics (how packs interact with API usage):
- Default: packs are consumed first (LIFO or FIFO?) — propose FIFO (oldest pack consumed first) to encourage frequent small purchases and avoid surprise consumption from old discounted packs.
- Multiple packs: allow per-route tagging so customers can route particular costs (e.g., embeddings draw from embedding packs).
- Partial consumption visibility: show burning rate in Console and apply per-route burn rates in Usage API.

Edge cases and leakage:
- Long-running streaming sessions can consume tokens at variable rate; need gating to prevent a single runaway session draining a large pre-paid pack without guardrails. Suggest per-session caps that can be configured by account.
- Model fallback: if a cheaper model is used automatically, burn rate should reflect model used (avoid cheap->expensive arbitrage by algorithmic routing).

Experiment ideas / metrics to track:
- Conversion funnel: % of trial users converting to packs vs PAYG. Track cohort by pack size recommended by UI.
- Retention: average days-until-second-purchase, average time-to-exhaust for each pack density.
- Elasticity: run A/B test on Starter price ±10% to estimate price elasticity for 10k packs.
- Churn risk: track accounts with 2+ months >50% unused balance.

Sample quick scenarios (back-of-envelope):
1) Small app (10k monthly tokens): Starter pack ($6.50) -> monthly revenue $6.50/user. If 1k customers, revenue = $6.5k/mo. Cost = 10k * 0.000225 * 1k = $2.25k/mo -> gross margin ≈ 65%.
2) High-usage client (1M tokens monthly): Pro pack amortized -> MSRP $50 per 100k -> they'd buy 10x = $500. Cost = 1M * 0.000225 = $225 -> margin ≈ 55%.

Operational notes / implementation time estimates:
- Metering change: pack-first billing + per-route burn attribution -> requires changes to billing microservice and usage-export pipeline. Estimated 3-5 sprints (infra + billing + console).
- Console UX: purchase flow, pack balance UI, recommendations card (when <60% of last pack remaining) -> 2 sprints.
- Fraud/KYC for large purchases -> coordinate with legal/payments team (1 sprint to spec).

Open questions / design decisions:
- Roll-over policy: expire vs slow-decay (e.g., -1% per month after 12 months) ? Pros/cons: expiry simplifies accounting, decay is fairer.
- Pricing anchor: should we expose $/token explicitly in UI or show only pack prices + examples? Tests show anchors matter; recommend both: show effective $/token in an expandable 'details' section.
- Should packs be model-specific (e.g., embedding packs) or universal with route filters? Model-specific packs simplify routing but fragment UX. Prefer universal packs with per-route allocation controls.

Next steps (immediate):
- Sync with infra to get updated blended cost per token (ticket: PRIC-879).
- Draft three UI mocks for purchase flow (Jon to take lead).
- Run quick elasticity experiment (Starter price +10% vs control) on 1-week cohort.

Notes to self / rough todo list:
- [ ] Confirm blended token/sec assumptions across small/medium/large models.
- [ ] Validate transaction fees and payment provider costs for small packs (impact on pocket margin).
- [ ] Propose pack rollover wording for legal review.
- [ ] Add example session vignettes with token counts for UX copy (10 examples: short-chat, long-chat, embeddings batch, summarization).

Random scribbles / thoughts:
- Could offer 'auto-pack compression' where we silently consolidate small leftover packs into a single higher-density pack on user opt-in. Might boost recency of purchases and reduce bookkeeping.
- Consider 'session reservations' where users reserve an estimated token amount for a large job (e.g., 50k tokens reserved for a nightly batch) — charges held in escrow.

References / links: see linked_artifacts above for PRIC-879 and slack thread.

End of notes.

Unresolved: confirm whether we want to make embedding packs distinct pricing bucket or keep unified. Personal lean: unified with tagging for simplicity.
